text: During a typhoon, mobile data can go down.
An emergency still needs a way to reach help.
With AGAP, a resident can send an SOS for themselves or someone nearby.
The alert includes the emergency type and location when available.
With a connection, the alert goes online.
When data drops, nearby participating phones can relay it over Bluetooth.
It can reach a responder or a phone that can get it online.
Responders can see where help is needed and coordinate who to send.
Status updates can let residents know help is on the way.
Residents get another way to ask for help.
Neighbors can relay alerts in the background.
Response teams get a clearer picture of where to act.
Get set up before an emergency.
AGAP. Built by the Fellowship for the Heroes of Innovation Challenge.
